OpenAI cut Luna API pricing by 80% this week, down to $0.20 per million input tokens. The cut comes from rewriting the code that serves GPT-5.6 Sol, which means you get the same model at a fifth of the old price.

Anthropic shipped Claude Opus 5 in the same week and kept its price at the $5 per million input tokens it already charged, and the new model matches or beats Fable 5 on most benchmarks. Google's Gemini 3.6 Flash finishes the same work using 17% fewer tokens, a saving that shows up as lower usage on your invoice. Google also split the tier further with a cheaper 3.5 Flash-Lite and a security-focused 3.5 Flash Cyber.

Price cuts in this market usually ride in on a new model release. A cut this size from serving code alone tells you the labs found room in their own infrastructure and are spending it on winning your workload.

So if you shelved a feature because inference was too expensive to run for every customer, price it again this week, because the math that killed it is out of date.

Your invoice will still depend on how many tokens you send and how often you retry, so expect the bill to fall by less than the 80% headline.

Which project would you bring back if inference cost a fifth of what it did a week ago?
